 Shailendra Sharma

 Appearance:
 Shri Virendra Singh Pal - Advocate for the applicant.

 Order

This third application filed by the applicant under Section 482 of BNSS 2023 (438 of the Cr.P.C.) for grant of anticipatory bail relating to Crime No.51/2021 registered at Police Station Indarganj,
District Gwalior (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 420, 468, 451(A) of IPC, Sections 45(S), 58(B)
and 5(A) of Reserve Bank of India Act, Section 3(6) of Nikshepakon Ke Hiton Ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam and Section 4(5)(6) of Chit Fund Money Banking Adhiniyam.

entities.text: Nikshepakon Ke Hiton Ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per prosecution case, applicant is the senior Assistant of company PACL Ltd.
He along-with co-accused took various amount from some different persons on the pretext of doubling the same but after the stipulated period, no amount has been given to the aggrieved persons.
Learned counsel for the present applicant submits that this is third bail application filed by the applicant.

Earlier first bail application of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:2569 2 MCRC-5831-2025 applicant was dismissed on merits vide order dated 02.01.2024 passed in M.Cr.C.No.57508/2023 and second bail application of the applicant was also dismissed on merits vide order dated 22.04.2024 passed in M.Cr.C.No.11675/2024.
He has filed this third bail application by claiming parity with co-accused persons namely Subhrat, Smt. Pushpa, Vikas and Sushil.
They have been granted bail by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide orders dated 31.10.2023 and 17.07.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.48902/2023 and M.Cr.C.No.28438/2023 respectively.
Learned counsel for the State has opposed the application on the ground that there is no change in the circumstances.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and after perusal of the record, it is found that after the said bail orders of co-accused persons, the first bail application of the present applicant was dismissed on merits vide order dated 02.01.2024.
Thereafter second bail application was also dismissed on 22.04.2024 finding no change in circumstance for second/subsequent bail application.
In this third bail application also there is no change in circumstances.
Learned counsel for the applicant could not point out any substantial change in circumstances enabling him to file this third/subsequent bail application.
Accordingly, the third application for anticipatory bail is dismissed.
(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE Monika Shailendra Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85083970/
